taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Bori-police-station, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 150 | 1.23 | 1.23
2 | 97.1 | 6.21 | 7.44
3 | 284 | 37.5 | 45
4 | 700 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Bori-police-station, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Bori-Police-Station, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted VES model for this station shows four layers with the following resistivity sequence: Layer 1 (150 Ω·m, 1.23 m thick), Layer 2 (97.1 Ω·m, 6.21 m thick), Layer 3 (284 Ω·m, 37.5 m thick), and Layer 4 (700 Ω·m, semi-infinite basement/aquifer zone).

Applying the standard curve-type notation: resistivity drops from Layer 1 to Layer 2, then rises from Layer 2 to Layer 3 (H-type for the first triplet), and continues rising from Layer 3 to Layer 4 (A-type for the second triplet). This gives a curve type of **HA**, not the **HK** type currently recorded in the file. An HK classification would require resistivity to decrease again after the third layer, which is not observed here (284 → 700 Ω·m is increasing). The on-file label should be corrected to HA to accurately reflect the subsurface resistivity trend for drilling planning purposes.

{"curve_type_stated": "HA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
